# Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#act-ambigsql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.00222v2) · arXiv v2, 27 July 2025

**Reading coverage:** All 45 pages: main sections 1–6; Appendices A–K, including AmbigSQL construction, all additional results, metrics, action/user-simulator prompts, qualitative failures, hyperparameters and assets.

## Research question

General conversational tuning does not reliably teach a model when to clarify, and limited conversation data can make action learning brittle.

## Method

ACT creates contrasting clarify/answer preferences, samples a response from the current policy, simulates its continuation, and replaces a winning or losing trajectory before a DPO update. AmbigSQL adds three synthetic underspecification types to paired Spider requests.

## Evaluation

Zephyr 7B is tuned with 50, 100 or 250 conversations and compared with SFT, preference baselines and larger prompted models on AmbigSQL, PACIFIC and Abg-CoQA. Separate action metrics and trajectory outcomes distinguish asking from actually solving; SQL outcomes use execution match.

## What the results support

On AmbigSQL with 50 conversations, ACT raises execution match from SFT’s 21.9% to 43.6%; gains shrink at 250 conversations. Larger prompted models still achieve higher SQL execution scores. Ablations on PACIFIC support contributions from action contrast, on-policy sampling and trajectory simulation.

## Limits and qualifications

Ambiguity is synthetically balanced and derived from a known target SQL. The SQL simulator sees that target and is instructed to rephrase the desired request, so measured recovery is not a human interaction study. Preference labels assume clarification timing is appropriate. Performance depends on commercial classifiers/simulators and task-specific outcome heuristics; the appendix reports inconsistent AmbigSQL beta values.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A concrete learning mechanism and paired benchmark for studying the distinction between recognizing a need to clarify and using clarification to recover an intended SQL query.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| ACT is the strongest SQL system overall. | ACT achieves 52.3% execution match with 250 conversations versus prompted Claude Sonnet 66.5%; the controlled comparison primarily concerns adaptation methods for Zephyr. | Table 3 and §5.2 | Restrict superiority to the specified tuning/data comparisons. |
| The appendix specifies an unambiguous AmbigSQL training beta. | Appendix J.2 assigns AmbigSQL both beta=0.01 and beta=0.5 in consecutive sentences. | Appendix J.2, p. 44 | Flag reproducibility ambiguity; do not choose a value without code-level confirmation. |
